wins.text: AI revenue surged 280% year-on-year to $3.1B in Q2, and full-year AI revenue guidance raised to over $11B
Consolidated Q2 revenue of $12.5B, up 43% YoY; organic (ex-VMware) revenue up 12% YoY
VMware ABV accelerated from $1.2B in Q1 to $1.9B in Q2; VMware spending run rate reduced to $1.6B/quarter from $2.3B pre-acquisition, targeting $1.2B post-integration — better than prior $1.4B plan
Networking revenue of $3.8B grew 44% YoY; full-year networking revenue growth guidance raised to 40% YoY from prior >35%

Infrastructure software operating margin at 64% ex-transition costs; VMware revenue on track toward $4B/quarter run rate with margins expected to converge to classic Broadcom software levels by FY2025

risks.text: Broadband revenue declined 39% YoY to $730M; full-year broadband guidance revised to down high-30s% YoY, worse than prior guidance of down just over 30%
Server storage connectivity revenue down 27% YoY to $824M; full-year decline now guided ~20% YoY
Industrial resale down 10% YoY; full-year now expected down double-digit % vs. prior high single-digit decline guidance
Gross margins for semiconductor segment compressed ~370 bps YoY to ~67%, driven by higher mix of custom AI accelerators with attached HBM memory diluting blended margins

Free cash flow as % of revenue declined YoY due to higher cash interest expense from $74B gross debt (VMware acquisition) and higher cash taxes from Section 174 delay; $74B gross debt remains a significant balance sheet overhang

guidance_items.detail: FY2024 consolidated revenue guidance raised to $51B (from prior guidance implied lower); driven by AI strength and VMware ramp
FY2024 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 61%
Full-year AI revenue guidance raised to over $11B; networking revenue growth guidance raised to 40% YoY from prior >35%
Broadband revenue now guided down high-30s% YoY vs. prior guidance of down just over 30% YoY
Industrial resale now guided down double-digit % YoY vs. prior high single-digit decline

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Competitive threat from NVIDIA in both custom AI accelerators and Ethernet switching (Spectrum-X)
Sustainability of gross margins in the custom AI accelerator business given HBM memory dilution and potential new ASIC competitors
Non-AI enterprise/hyperscaler networking inventory correction and timing of recovery
